_: The Anchorframe intake: the questions every new project answers before Stage 1. Generic on purpose; a project's proposed answers live in projects/<slug>/intake.json. The studio page renders both, saves the answers in its shared store, and Claude writes them into project.json on sync. `feeds` names the project.json field an answer fills.

questions.q: What is this film made from, and do you hold the rights to it?
questions.why: Everything downstream is checked against the source: attribution, order, names. Upload the manuscript and any screenplay pages under Uploads → Source.

questions.q: Which part of the source does this film cover?
questions.why: Chapters, scenes or pages. It sets what the short keeps and what the long episode puts back.

questions.q: What is the film about, in one sentence?
questions.why: The logline. If it needs a second sentence, the film has two subjects.

questions.q: Who changes, and in which shot is their last held close-up?
questions.why: The turn. The last held close-up belongs to whoever changes; the board is built toward it.

questions.q: Do the prompts use the source's names or production names?
questions.why: Prompts are published with the film on most festival pages. Production names keep the film and the book apart in public; source names keep the adaptation honest.
One shot pool cuts to every length, but the first form decides the rhythm: held frames for a short, montage for a music video.

questions.q: Where will it be shown, under what rules, and by when?
questions.why: Venue, rules, and the deadline in its own timezone. Episode 1 had two records that disagreed on the timezone.

questions.q: What aspect, resolution and frame rate?
questions.why: Set once. The timeline must match before export or the bars bake in.

questions.q: What should each movement look like?
questions.why: One lighting plate per movement; every frame inherits its plate. Upload reference images under Uploads → Look.

questions.q: Which of your tracks go with which song or cue?
questions.why: Lock the song before the stills reel; the cut will follow the lyrics. Paste Suno links or track names with their tempo.

questions.q: Who speaks, and with what voice?
questions.why: Generated voices per line, your own recordings, or none. Dialogue is routed into shots as audio references, never the model's own audio.

questions.q: Which characters need a trained Soul, and which can be elements only?
questions.why: A Soul holds one face across solo shots; two-person shots run on elements. Upload any reference art under Uploads → Cast.

questions.q: What carries over from the previous film by id?
questions.why: Places, plates and faces that already exist are attached by their old ids, never described again.

questions.q: How many credits will you spend this round, and on what?
questions.why: Images are cheap and video is not. The Higgsfield tab shows the live balance and every Generate button previews its cost first.

questions.q: Who else works on this, and what do they do?
questions.why: Anyone you share the studio with at Contributor or above can answer, upload and log takes.

questions.q: What does done look like for this round, and by when?
questions.why: Name the gate you are aiming at. A gate is a person looking at a screen, recorded.
